questions.solution:
The relation is $n^3+n$: $7^3+7=343+7=350$.
So the missing term is $9^3+9=729+9=$ **738**. (729 = 9³ alone is the trap.)

**Answer: 738**
questions.shortcut: Spot 350 = 343 + 7 = 7³ + 7; apply the same cube-plus-n to 9.

questions.q: **PALM : QBMN :: LIME : ?**
questions.solution:
Every letter moves one step forward: P→Q, A→B, L→M, M→N.
Applying +1 to LIME gives L→M, I→J, M→N, E→F = **MJNF**.

**Answer: MJNF**
questions.shortcut: Verify the shift on the first letter pair (P→Q = +1) and slide the whole word.

questions.q: **Find the odd one out: 64, 125, 216, 342**
questions.solution:
64 = 4³, 125 = 5³, 216 = 6³ are perfect cubes.
342 is not a cube — the next cube is $7^3 = 343$, which makes 342 a near-miss trap.

**Answer: 342**
questions.shortcut: Scan cubes of 4, 5, 6, 7 — 342 sits just below 343 and breaks the pattern.

questions.q: **Find the odd one out: ACE, BDF, CEG, DEI**
questions.solution:
ACE, BDF and CEG each skip one letter between consecutive letters (+2, +2).
In DEI, D→E is +1 and E→I is +4 — the pattern breaks, so **DEI** is the odd cluster.

**Answer: DEI**
questions.shortcut: Check the gap between the first two letters of each cluster first; DEI fails immediately.

questions.q: **Find the next term: 5, 11, 23, 47, 95, ?**
questions.solution:
Each term is double the previous one plus 1: $5\times2+1=11$, $11\times2+1=23$, and so on.
Next term: $95\times2+1=$ **191**.

**Answer: 191**
questions.shortcut: Differences are 6, 12, 24, 48 — doubling. Add 48 to 95? No: apply ×2+1 to get 191.

questions.q: **Find the next term: 100, 96, 87, 71, 46, ?**
questions.solution:
Subtract successive terms: $-4, -9, -16, -25$ — perfect squares $2^2, 3^2, 4^2, 5^2$.
Next subtraction is $6^2=36$: $46-36=$ **10**.

**Answer: 10**
questions.shortcut: When drops grow steadily, test square numbers 4, 9, 16, 25 before anything else.

questions.q: **Find the next term: AZ, CX, EV, ?**
questions.solution:
First letters: A, C, E, … (+2 each) → next is **G**.
Second letters: Z, X, V, … (−2 each) → next is **T**.
The next term is **GT**.

**Answer: GT**
questions.shortcut: Handle the two letter slots independently — both move by 2 in opposite directions.

questions.q: **In a certain code, FAMOUS is written as 6113152119. How will DANGER be written in that code?**
questions.solution:
Each letter is replaced by its alphabet position, written together:
F=6, A=1, M=13, O=15, U=21, S=19 → 6-1-13-15-21-19 = 6113152119.
DANGER: D=4, A=1, N=14, G=7, E=5, R=18 → **41147518**.

**Answer: 41147518**
questions.shortcut: Split the code as 6 | 1 | 13 | 15 | 21 | 19 — two-digit values reveal the letter-position code.

questions.q: **In a certain language, 'sky is blue' is coded as 'pa ta ma', 'sea is deep' as 'ra ta ka', and 'sea waves' as 'ra na'. What is the code for 'is'?**
questions.solution:
'is' is the only word common to the first two sentences, and 'ta' is the only code common to their codes.
So 'is' = **ta**. ('ra' belongs to 'sea', shared by the last two.)

**Answer: ta**
questions.shortcut: Match the common word of two sentences with the common code of the same two sentences.

questions.q: **A wooden cube of side 7 cm is painted on all its faces and then cut into small cubes of side 1 cm. How many of the small cubes have exactly two faces painted?**
questions.solution:
Exactly two painted faces = cubes from the edges (not corners).
Each of the 12 edges gives $7-2=5$ such cubes.
Total $=12\times5=$ **60**.

**Answer: 60**
questions.shortcut: Edge cubes = 12 × (n − 2); corners give three faces, face-centres give one.

questions.q: **If 'A' means '×', 'B' means '÷', 'C' means '+' and 'D' means '−', then 15 B 3 C 8 A 4 D 12 A 2 = ?**
questions.solution:
Replace the letters: $15\div3+8\times4-12\times2$.
By BODMAS: $5+32-24=13$.

**Answer: 13**
questions.shortcut: Rewrite with symbols first, then do ÷ and × before + and −.

questions.q: **By interchanging the signs '+' and '×' and also the numbers 4 and 6, which of the following equations becomes correct?**
questions.solution:
Swap '+'↔'×' and 4↔6 throughout each option, then check.
$6\times4+3=22$ becomes $4+6\times3=22$, i.e. $4+18=22$ — correct.
The others give $32\ne38$, $33\ne20$ and $33\ne35$.

**Answer: 6 × 4 + 3 = 22**
questions.shortcut: Swap in place, then evaluate the × parts before the + parts — one option survives.

questions.solution:
In each row, first ÷ second = third: $48\div12=4$ and $81\div9=9$.
So $63\div7=$ **9**.

**Answer: 9**
questions.shortcut: Test the simplest row operation (÷) on the two complete rows; it holds in both.

questions.q: **A is the brother of B. B is the sister of C. D is the father of C. How is A related to D?**
questions.solution:
A, B and C are siblings (A brother of B, B sister of C).
D is the father of C, so D is the father of A too. A is male, so A is D's **son**.

**Answer: Son**
questions.shortcut: 'Brother of' and 'sister of' both mean the pair shares parents — the three are one sibling set.

questions.q: **If P + Q means 'P is the father of Q', P − Q means 'P is the mother of Q', and P × Q means 'P is the brother of Q', then in the expression A + B × C − D, how is A related to D?**
questions.solution:
A + B: A is the father of B. B × C: B is the brother of C, so A is C's father as well.
C − D: C is the mother of D. A is the father of C, so A is D's mother's father — the **grandfather** (maternal).

**Answer: Grandfather**
questions.shortcut: Split the expression at each symbol: father → brother → mother; count generations down from A.

questions.q: **A man walks 8 km towards north, turns left and walks 6 km, turns left again and walks 8 km, then turns right and walks 6 km. How far and in which direction is he from his starting point?**
questions.solution:
Path: north 8 → west 6 → south 8 → west 6.
North and south cancel; net movement is $6+6=12$ km towards **west**.

**Answer: 12 km, west**
questions.shortcut: The 8 km north and 8 km south legs cancel — only the two west legs add up.

questions.q: **A person walks 10 m towards east, turns to his left and walks 8 m, turns left again and walks 6 m, then turns to his right and walks 4 m, and finally turns right and walks 8 m. How far is he from his starting point?**
questions.solution:
Path: east 10 → north 8 → west 6 → north 4 → east 8.
Net east $=10-6+8=12$; net north $=8+4=12$.
Distance $=\sqrt{12^2+12^2}=12\sqrt2$ m.

**Answer: $12\sqrt{2}$ m**
questions.shortcut: Add up east–west and north–west separately; equal legs of 12 give $12\sqrt2$ at once.

questions.q: **In a row of 55 students, P is 16th from the left end and Q is 20th from the right end. If P and Q interchange their positions, what will be P's position from the left end?**
questions.solution:
After swapping, P takes Q's place.
Q's position from the left $=55-20+1=36$.
So P becomes **36th** from the left end.

**Answer: 36th**
questions.shortcut: Convert Q's right-end rank to a left-end rank; P's original rank (16th) is extra information.

questions.q: **Five friends A, B, C, D and E compare their heights. A is taller than C but shorter than B. E is taller than B. D is taller than E. Who is the second tallest?**
questions.solution:
Chain the clues: B > A > C, E > B, D > E.
Combining: D > E > B > A > C.
The second tallest is **E**.

**Answer: E**
questions.shortcut: String the comparisons into one chain (D > E > B > A > C) instead of drawing a chart.

questions.q: **Eight friends A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H sit in a row facing north. H sits at the extreme left end and C at the extreme right end. D sits second from the left end. G sits immediately to the right of D. B, F and A sit together in that order. E sits immediately to the right of A. Who sits third to the left of C?**
questions.solution:
Fix H = 1, D = 2, G = 3, C = 8. The block B-F-A must occupy three consecutive seats with E just after A.
Seats 4–7 remain, so B = 4, F = 5, A = 6, E = 7.
Row: H · D · G · B · F · A · E · C. Third to the left of C (seat 8) is seat 5 = **F**.

**Answer: F**
questions.shortcut: Lock the fixed seats, then the 'B, F, A together in that order' block can only start at seat 4.

questions.q: **Six friends P, Q, R, S, T and U sit equally spaced around a circular table, all facing the centre. P sits second to the left of R. Q sits immediately to the right of P. S sits opposite Q. U sits second to the left of T. Who sits exactly opposite T?**
questions.solution:
Facing the centre, 'left' is clockwise and 'right' is anticlockwise.
Fix R. P is second left of R; Q is immediately right of P; S lands opposite Q; the last two seats go to T and U, and 'U second to the left of T' fixes them.
Clockwise order: R · Q · P · T · S · U. Opposite T is **R**.

**Answer: R**
questions.shortcut: For centre-facing circles: left = clockwise, right = anticlockwise. Fix one person and chain the clues.

questions.q:
**Statements: Some cars are buses. All buses are trucks. No truck is a cycle.**

**Conclusions:** I. Some cars are trucks. II. No bus is a cycle.
questions.solution:
I: the cars that are buses are also trucks (all buses are trucks), so some cars are trucks — follows.
II: every bus is a truck, and no truck is a cycle, so no bus can be a cycle — follows.

**Answer: Both conclusions follow**
questions.shortcut: Chain statements sharing a term: cars→buses→trucks→cycles settles both conclusions.

questions.q:
**Statements: All keys are locks. No lock is a door. Some doors are windows.**

**Conclusions:** I. No key is a door. II. Some windows are locks.
questions.solution:
I: keys sit inside locks, and no lock is a door, so no key is a door — follows.
II: the statement chain never connects windows to locks (only doors link them, and locks exclude doors) — 'some windows are locks' is not certain, so it does not follow.

**Answer: Only conclusion I follows**
questions.shortcut: Keys→locks→(not doors): the chain stops at doors, so any window–lock claim fails.

questions.q: **In a survey of 100 people, 62 read newspaper H and 48 read newspaper T. If 10 people read neither paper, how many people read exactly one of the two newspapers?**
questions.solution:
Read at least one $=100-10=90$.
Read both $=62+48-90=20$.
Exactly one $=90-20=$ **70**.

**Answer: 70**
questions.shortcut: Exactly one = (sum of singles) − 2 × (both) = 110 − 40 = 70.

questions.q:
**Arrange the following words as they would appear in an English dictionary:**

1. Kiln  2. Kindly  3. Kitten  4. Kind  5. Kingdom
questions.solution:
Compare letter by letter: Kiln (Kil…) comes before all Kin… words (l < n).
Among the Kin… words: Kind < Kindly (shorter word first) < Kingdom (d < g) < Kitten (n < t).
Order: Kiln, Kind, Kindly, Kingdom, Kitten = **1, 4, 2, 5, 3**.

**Answer: 1, 4, 2, 5, 3**
questions.shortcut: Sort by the third letter first (l < n < t) — only the Kin… group needs deeper comparison.

questions.q:
**Statement: 'All students of Class X who cleared the pre-board examination will receive a scholarship.' — notice by the school principal**

**Conclusions:** I. Some students of Class X who cleared the pre-board examination will receive a scholarship. II. Students of Class X who did not clear the pre-board examination will not receive the scholarship.
questions.solution:
I: 'all' necessarily includes 'some' (the group is real, as stated by the notice) — follows.
II: the notice says nothing about students who did not clear; that is the inverse of the given statement, which is not logically valid — does not follow.

**Answer: Only conclusion I follows**
questions.shortcut: 'All A are B' guarantees 'some A are B' but never 'non-A are not B'.

questions.q:
**Statement: 'Passengers are requested to fasten their seat belts before take-off.' — announcement inside an aircraft**

**Conclusions:** I. Passengers generally do not fasten their seat belts unless asked. II. Take-off is the most dangerous part of a flight.
questions.solution:
A request is a safety instruction; it does not establish what passengers generally do, so I does not follow.
II adds a claim about danger that the announcement never makes — it does not follow.
Neither conclusion is a definite inference from the statement.

**Answer: Neither conclusion follows**
questions.shortcut: A request or instruction implies no general behaviour claim — reject both habit and danger inferences.

questions.q: **Which of the following words will look exactly the same as the word when its reflection in water (image in a horizontal mirror placed below it) is seen?**
questions.solution:
A water image flips letters top-to-bottom, so every letter must be symmetric about a horizontal line.
O, X, I, D, E all pass this test, so **OXIDE** is unchanged. M, V and S (in the other words) are not horizontally symmetric.

**Answer: OXIDE**
questions.shortcut: Horizontal-symmetric letters: B, C, D, E, H, I, K, O, X — one asymmetric letter kills the word.

questions.q: **A circular sheet of paper is folded exactly in half along a diameter, and then folded again along the perpendicular diameter. Two holes are then punched through the folded quarter-circle, neither touching a fold line. How many holes will the fully opened sheet have?**
questions.solution:
Two perpendicular folds create $2\times2=4$ layers.
Each punch goes through all 4 layers, and each unfolds into one hole.
Total holes $=4\times2=$ **8** (in four symmetric pairs).

**Answer: 8**
questions.shortcut: Holes = layers at the punch × punches; each fold doubles the layer count.

questions.q: **How many triangles are there in the figure below?**
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="100" height="100" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><rect x="10" y="10" width="80" height="80"/><line x1="10" y1="10" x2="90" y2="90"/><line x1="90" y1="10" x2="10" y2="90"/></svg>
questions.solution:
The two diagonals meet at the centre, creating 4 small triangles around it.
Each half of the square (split by one diagonal) is a large triangle: 4 more.
Total $=4+4=$ **8**.

**Answer: 8**
questions.shortcut: Square with both diagonals always gives 8 triangles: 4 small + 4 half-square.
